outcome_branch: early rejection at performance-leadership.md section 6 step 2: the redundant accounting pass and the group position scan are each below 1% of the named cells; remaining implementation criteria do not apply
hypothesis: fetch_records sums fetched bytes and then walks the same records again for per-topic metrics, and group poll rebuilds delivered positions by scanning assignment against the pending queues. Fusing the walks and caching positions was expected to cut CPU on nb-fetch-bulk and nb-fetch-capped-paused.
finding: Both named cells use Consumer::fetch, so positions() and record_delivered_positions are not on the measured path. One bulk round returns 135000 records and costs 59.498 ms of client CPU. A release-optimized replica of the two-pass accounting versus one fused pass saved 181 µs and 357 µs (0.30% and 0.60% of that round). The two-pass block itself is 2.13–2.37 ms because the bytes still have to be counted once. Capped-paused accounting across 2000 one-record polls was 75 µs, 0.14% of 52.073 ms of poll CPU. A six-partition position clone scan was 0.5 µs. Fusing does not change the per-round topic-metric HashMap, so bulk allocations stay 135451. No production code was changed.
host: Intel Xeon family 6 model 207, 4 cores, Linux 6.12.94+ x86_64, frequency unpinned (harness 2400 MHz), rustc 1.99.0 (b940084d7 2026-09-28), release profile

primary.metric: redundant fetched-byte pass, ns saved versus one fused pass, as a percent of nb-fetch-bulk client CPU
primary.note: Cell repetitions are one parent run per cell. The accounting delta is two opt-level=3 microbench runs over 135000 records, not an interleaved candidate.

results.correctness: no production diff; remaining suites do not apply on this rejection branch

limits: Local unsigned measurement. Not a Kafka throughput comparison. Suite HOLD remains active.
